title: Privilege slicing and hierarchical resource model with enriched audit context
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Design and deliver the RBAC v2 role model covering: a compact hierarchical resource identifier scheme, fine-grained scope types (invoke/read/write/admin), role composition semantics, and an audit-event schema that supports downstream SIEM and compliance exports. This ticket consolidates decisions for engineering implementation and provides migration guidance from the v1 flat-permission model. The goal is a high-performance, cache-friendly authorization API that preserves strong auditability and supports SSO/SAML mapping and SCIM provisioning.
acceptance_criteria: Formal resource hierarchy defined and documented (URN format + examples) for Account / Organization / Workspace / Environment / Model / Endpoint
Permission taxonomy (operation -> scope) defined with a canonical permissions matrix and example role bundles
Audit event schema defined with mandatory fields for compliance (actor, roles, action, resource, before/after, request_id, correlation_id, auth_mechanism, session_id, source_ip, timestamp)
API contract for policy evaluation endpoints documented (inputs, outputs, error modes) and implemented with unit tests
Backwards-compatible migration plan with data transformation scripts and a phased rollout plan (canary + org opt-in + full switch) documented
Performance targets captured: cached check median <5ms, cold eval median <50ms; auth cache hit-rate telemetry instrumented
Security review sign-off received and SCIM/SSO mapping patterns documented
End-to-end e2e test harness demonstrating role updates invalidating cache and generating audit events
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting with PM, Security, and DevRel. Agreed on primary hierarchy: account:org:workspace:env:model:endpoint. Decided to use compact URN style (r:<type>:<id>...) for efficient prefix matching.
2026-02-25: Prototype of URN prefix-matching in runtime router. Early perf looks good; prefix lookup uses radix tree for O(k) match where k is token count.
2026-03-01: Security review feedback: include auth_mechanism and token_hash in audit event, require session_id for JIT elevation events. Added to schema draft.
2026-03-04: PM requested explicit support for organization-scoped role overrides (org-admin that cannot escalate to account-admin). Added 'scope_bound_admin' concept and edge-case rules.
2026-03-08: Design review with SDK team: introduced /v1/authz/check bulk endpoint to support batching of 50 checks in single call; SDK will add helper for local caching with invalidation on webhooks.

2026-03-12: Decided on migration strategy: two-phase. Phase 1: server-side evaluation supports both v1 and v2 schemas with feature-flag per org. Phase 2: backfill roles to v2 canonical and flip default. Created migration job spec (link below).
2026-03-12: Open questions: TTL for positive cache (default 30s vs 5s for high-risk operations), and break-glass audit retention policy. Security to propose defaults by 2026-03-19.
design_notes: Key decisions: (1) use compact URN 'r:<type>:<id>[:<sub>...]' for hierarchical resolution and efficient prefix queries in routing. (2) Introduce scope slices: invoke, read, write, admin, and 'audit-only' for read-of-audit. (3) Roles are composable sets of scope bindings (resource-pattern -> set(scopes)), with explicit deny taking precedence. (4) Implement role-versioning: each role binding has a monotonic version to allow fast invalidation across runtime nodes.
audit_schema: Mandatory event fields: timestamp, event_id, request_id, correlation_id, actor_id, actor_email, actor_roles (list), actor_role_versions (list), action, resource_urn, resource_type, resource_owner_account, scope, outcome (allow/deny), reason, before_state (redacted), after_state (redacted), auth_mechanism (SAML|OAuth|APIKey), saml_assertion_id (optional), session_id, token_hash, source_ip, user_agent, service_node_id. Events should be emitted to Kafka topic 'audit.events.v2' with JSON-lines. Retention policies managed by Compliance team.
sso_saml_provisioning: Primary mapping model: SAML group -> role canonical name. Support attribute-based role assignment via SAML Attribute 'roles' and SCIM group imports for persistent membership. For unaffiliated orgs use email-domain fallback mapping. Documented claim names and required attributes for SAML IdPs. Support single-attribute 'role_path' that maps to resource-scoped role (e.g., 'org:acme:org-admin').
admin_controls: Controls include: break-glass emergency tokens (time-limited, fully auditable), JIT elevation flow requiring approval in Console for sensitive scopes, session-scoped temporary roles (ttl), enforced MFA for role elevation, and separation-of-duty checks when creating top-level roles. Console will expose 'role-simulator' UI to preview effective permissions and the audit trail for simulate runs must be logged.
migration_plan: Phase A (canary, 4 weeks): support dual-evaluation (v1/v2) behind org feature-flag; provide admin UI to preview converted roles. Phase B (backfill, 2 weeks): run backfill jobs that convert v1 role sets into canonical v2 bindings; validate via fuzzy tests; Phase C (flip): enable v2 by default and deprecate v1 (announcements, 30-day opt-out). Provide rollback path by preserving v1 mapping and toggling flag.
api_contract_examples: POST /v1/authz/check body: {actor_id, checks: [{resource_urn, action}], context: {request_id, correlation_id}} -> response: {results: [{resource_urn, action, allowed, reasons}], cache_hint: {ttl_seconds}}. Errors: 429 for rate-limit, 503 degraded if policy-store unavailable. Bulk endpoint supports up to 50 checks per call. SDKs should expose checkBatch and onRoleChange hooks.
performance_considerations: Auth cache design: per-actor + resource_prefix + action key with default TTL 30s. Strong invalidation on role-change events via role_version publish on the role-update Kafka topic. Metrics: auth_check.latency_ms (p50/p95), auth_cache.hit_rate, role_update.propagation_lag_ms. Target propagation lag < 2s for critical role changes in Dedicated deployments.
open_risks: 1) Revocation window: if cache TTL is long, revoked privileges may persist briefly. Mitigation: publish immediate invalidation events and use short TTL for admin scopes. 2) SAML mapping complexity across IdPs may require vendor-by-vendor docs. 3) Audit log volume increase—ensure ingestion pipeline and retention quotas are supported.
next_steps: 1) Security to finalize TTL and retention defaults (due 2026-03-19). 2) Infra to prototype radix-tree prefix router and push PR. 3) SDK team to implement checkBatch helper and local cache with invalidation hook. 4) Schedule migration dry-run for 2026-03-28.
